messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: generated quantities only after warmup?
parts:
Hello,

I am unsure if the generated quantities block is 
executed during warmup, or only after warmup is finished.
The manual sais it is executed once per sample, but I am unsure if iteration "samples" are also samples ...
Which is true?

In case the generated quantities block is executed during warmup, 
is there a way to change this behavior so that generated quantities 
are only calculated after warmup (in cmdstan)?

Best -- Guido

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] generated quantities only after warmup?
parts:
Yes, generated quantities are executed during warmup. Otherwise, there's
no way to produce plots, etc. It's a bit of a pain because if the generated
quantities crash during warmup, it stops sampling.

The way you could have tested this would be to set up something that
only does warmup and include a print statement.

- Bob

P.S. That should say "once per iteration" not "once per sample".
Andrew's been on me not to conflate a sample (a set of draws)
with a single draw, but it's still making its way through all of
our broken doc.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] generated quantities only after warmup?
parts:
> On Oct 13, 2015, at 5:07 PM, Guido Biele <guido...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Thanks for the info,
>
> the problem isn't that anything is crashing, but that I calculate average predictive comparisons in the generated quantities. This is very slow because it involves computing pairwise comparisons between data points. Therefor I would have liked to avoid computing them during the warmup.
>
> I believe I once read a request to expose the iteration number so that it could be used to determine which section of a program is executed. But if I remember correctly this was not implemented because there were reasons not to do this.
>
> So in conclusion it looks as if I just have to live with the fact that the generated quantities block is also executed during warmup.
>
> Is this correct?

Yes it is.

The reason not to remove values from warmup iterations
is that if they're not there, all of our posterior tools
will crash and burn.

The reason we don't want to expose iteration number and/or
chain ID is that it's not part of the log density abstraction
we've made --- we think of a Stan model plus data as being
something that given uncontrained parameter values, computes
log density and gradients. If we add things in the language
th pick out iteration numbers, then we have to hack them in
places where there aren't iterations, such as when used
in diagnostics or in external calls from R.

- Bob

messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] generated quantities only after warmup?
parts:
I agree with Ben!

If I find that i have a stable model (i.e. a model that converges well), 
I tend not to save the warmup samples/iterations.

I'll just add an issue to the stan repository and hope for the best ;-).

Just to give an example of how burdensome unnecessary calculation 
of the generated quantities can be when calculating average predictive comparisons (APC)*:

Lets assume one does a multiple regression with 5 predictor variables and n=1000.
To do APCs one calculates for each predictor variable all pairwise comparisons
of the y_hats for all cases (I am simplifying a bit here...). This means next to 2.5 million 
pairwise comparisons per sample/iteration. 
Unfortunately, my analyses involve around  20 predictors and 40000 cases. 
So even though I am doing a hierarchical model and the number of pairwise comparisons 
is reduced because comparisons happen only within subgroups, a lot of 
pairwise comparisons are calculated in the generated quantities block. 

Therefor the possibility to turn of calculation of generated quantities when 
warmup samples/iterations are not saved would be very much appreciated.


Guido


*www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/published/ape17.pdf

Cheers - Guido

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] generated quantities only after warmup?
parts:
Hi!

As a workaround you could just not do any calculations during the warmup+sampling phase, but do the simulations later on in R. Using the expose_stan_functions facility you can take advantage of all code you wrote as Stan user functions.

I am doing that all the time since my models just run too long and I do not want to wait for another model run whenever I want to simulate something new.

Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] generated quantities only after warmup?
parts:
What I'm going to work on next after general indexing (almost done!)
is something to let you run a Stan model, then run a second generated
quantities block on the output. Hopefully we'll then be able to put
the two things together into a single output, but that's an interface
issue more than an underlying Stan sampling issue.

Turning off generated quantities could work if no warmup draws
are saved. In fact, we probably should do that as a matter of course.
The only time it could hurt is if you have a bad generated quantities
block, spend a long time in warmup only to discover there's a bug
in the generated quantities.

If 99% of your work's done in generated quantities and you
ran with half warmup, half sampling iterations, you'd save 49.5%
of the time not executing generated quantities during warmup.

- Bob
